paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.VerbTricolon = NO --> The study compares recordings of hippocampal place cells from bats flying through tunnels, rats moving over an arena floor, and bats flying through a room. For tunnel flights, the analysis uses distance along an approximately one-dimensional route, although the tunnel itself has width and height. The floor map uses two position coordinates, and the room map uses three. <!-- vale ai-tells.VerbTricolon = YES -->

review.purpose: Identify species, environments and position dimensions.
review.connection: Supplies the concrete recordings behind the variety in p7.
review.reason: A tunnel has physical width but the analyzed route is one dimensional.

paragraphs.text: A cell recorded on a short track may have one smooth firing hill. [On a long track, the same kind of cell may have several separated fields, each with a different width and height. In a room, its active regions can bend, split, and surround inactive holes. How could one model produce this variety and still make useful predictions?]{.key-statement}

review.purpose: Ask how one model explains multiple shapes and sizes.
review.connection: Turns the environment list into the problem answered by p9.
review.reason: The contrast with a short-track hill makes the modeling need understandable.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.EmptyPadding = NO --> <!-- vale ai-tells.StrawmanContrast = NO --> Mainali, Azeredo da Silveira, and Burak propose that a cell's spatial input is a smooth random function. This function can be interpreted as the average combined input arriving through the cell's synapses at each animal position. The model cell has positive firing rate where this input exceeds a threshold. The recordings estimate firing rates rather than measuring this input directly.[^p3-model] [The model predicts distributions of field lengths, areas, and volumes, rather than the location of a particular cell's next field. Its strongest tests check whether fitting field sizes and counts also explains field shapes and holes.]{.key-statement}[^p3-question] <!-- vale ai-tells.StrawmanContrast = YES --> <!-- vale ai-tells.EmptyPadding = YES -->

review.purpose: Connect summed synaptic input, threshold and measured firing.
review.connection: Answers p7 with a candidate mechanism before naming a process.
review.reason: The measured rate versus unobserved input distinction limits later biological claims.

paragraphs.text: We begin on a track, where a field starts at [an [**upcrossing**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}, a point where the input crosses upward through the threshold.]{.definition-explanation} Counting these crossings gives the average number of fields. Combining that count with the lengths of active fields and inactive gaps then separates the effect of the threshold from the distance over which the map changes. These calculations establish the parameters needed for the later predictions of sizes and shapes.

review.purpose: Introduce upcrossings and the count-to-parameter route.
review.connection: Uses thresholding to motivate the first one-dimensional calculation.
review.reason: The crossing has a physical meaning before the formula.

paragraphs.text: [Spatial randomness here describes different possible rate maps. Once a map is drawn, it is fixed while the animal moves through it. The spatial coordinate is not time, and the model does not by itself describe memory drift, spike timing, or learning.]{.key-statement}

review.purpose: Fix the spatial ensemble versus temporal-motion distinction.
review.connection: Closes the opening before the Gaussian map definition.
review.reason: The preceding eye and memory chapters could otherwise suggest changing maps.

paragraphs.text: To predict a field's width, we need to relate activity at nearby positions. A histogram of firing rates alone loses that information: rearranging its values could turn one broad field into many tiny fields without changing the histogram.

review.purpose: Show why a rate histogram cannot predict field width.
review.connection: Raises the missing dependence information supplied by p23.
review.reason: Rearranging values is a direct counterexample needing no extra theory.

paragraphs.text: The model assigns an input $h(x)$ to each position $x$, with nearby values linked so that a cell can have a continuous active region. [A [**Gaussian process**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} specifies a distribution of such maps.]{.definition-explanation} Its mean sets the average input, and its spatial covariance describes how inputs at two positions vary together across possible maps. The chosen covariance must also make the maps smooth enough for the derivatives used below. After a map is drawn, moving the animal changes which position is evaluated, not the map itself.

review.purpose: Describe a map draw, covariance and position evaluation.
review.connection: Answers p21 and introduces the formal definition fold.
review.reason: The visible text explains the physical operation before optional formal detail.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = NO --> [A Gaussian process is a probability distribution over functions such that the values at any finite set of positions form a jointly Gaussian random vector.]{.definition-explanation} For positions $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, the vector $(h(x_1),\ldots,h(x_n))$ therefore has a multivariate Gaussian distribution. Its mean vector and covariance matrix are obtained by evaluating two functions, <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = YES -->

review.purpose: Define finite joint Gaussian values and the mean/covariance functions.
review.connection: Expands p23 inside the mathematical-definition fold.
review.reason: The exact distributional definition supports readers checking Gaussian calculations.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = NO --> The expectation runs over possible maps, or over cells assumed to share these statistics. These two functions determine every finite joint distribution. A Gaussian process can thus produce many different curves while keeping a precise rule for their spatial dependence. [A [**jointly Gaussian vector**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} is one for which every linear combination of its entries is Gaussian.]{.definition-explanation} For this family, zero covariance between two subvectors implies their independence. That extra property, which does not hold for general distributions, will simplify the crossing calculation. The values after thresholding will generally not have a Gaussian distribution.[^p3-model] <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = YES -->

review.purpose: Explain the ensemble average and Gaussian independence property.
review.connection: Interprets the preceding mean/covariance display, then prepares crossing simplification.
review.reason: It distinguishes Gaussian input from rectified firing values.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.CataphoricForecasting = NO --> Three assumptions have different jobs: <!-- vale ai-tells.CataphoricForecasting = YES -->

review.purpose: Introduce separate roles for the next assumptions.
review.connection: Connects the process definition to stationarity, isotropy and smoothness.
review.reason: The short lead-in is completed by its actual list.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.EmptyPadding = NO -->

review.purpose: Hidden lint control: ai-tells.EmptyPadding NO.
review.connection: Placed after p42 and before p47; it changes diagnostic scope, not the reader argument.
review.reason: The comment delimiters hide this control from prose. Its placement was read with the adjacent passage and does not substitute for teaching.

paragraphs.text: [[**Stationarity**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} means that moving the observation window does not change the map's probability law. Here it gives a constant mean and a covariance $C(x,y)=C(y-x)$ that depends on separation.]{.definition-explanation} It does not say that a particular map is flat. <!-- vale ai-tells.EmptyPadding = YES --> <!-- vale ai-tells.ParallelStaccato = NO -->

review.purpose: Define translation-invariant spatial statistics.
review.connection: First of the assumptions, before covariance is reduced to separation.
review.reason: It prevents confusing stationarity with a flat realization.

paragraphs.text: [[**Isotropy**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} means that rotating the separation does not change the covariance: in several dimensions, $C(\Delta x)$ depends only on $\|\Delta x\|$.]{.definition-explanation} It rules out a preferred direction in the model's statistics. Stationarity alone does not imply isotropy. <!-- vale ai-tells.ParallelStaccato = YES -->

review.purpose: Define rotation-invariant dependence.
review.connection: Separates directional symmetry from the preceding translation condition.
review.reason: Later multidimensional curvature uses this additional assumption.

paragraphs.text: [[**Smoothness**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} controls whether the map has well defined spatial derivatives.]{.definition-explanation} Crossing calculations require differentiable sample functions and nondegenerate joint distributions: the relevant vector of heights and derivatives must have an invertible covariance matrix, rather than obey an exact linear constraint. Peak calculations require second derivatives and enough regularity to control their local approximation.

review.purpose: State derivative and nondegeneracy requirements.
review.connection: Completes the assumption list before any derivative calculation.
review.reason: Crossing and peak arguments require different derivative orders.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = NO --> A Gaussian distribution of values does not guarantee this smoothness. For example, a covariance proportional to $e^{-|x-y|/b}$ has a sharp corner at zero separation and does not supply the differentiable paths assumed below. <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = YES -->

review.purpose: Give a Gaussian covariance that lacks the needed smoothness.
review.connection: Tests p52 before adopting the smooth model.
review.reason: The counterexample prevents deriving differentiability from Gaussian values alone.

paragraphs.text: Set the mean to zero and write $\sigma_h^2=C(0)$ for input variance. A constant input mean can be absorbed into the threshold. It is useful to normalize the input,

review.purpose: Normalize the input and absorb a constant mean into threshold.
review.connection: Moves from assumptions to the firing-rule display.
review.reason: It explains the transformation rather than merely introducing new symbols.

paragraphs.text: Here $z$ has variance one, $q$ is a dimensionless threshold, and $a>0$ converts normalized input to firing rate, in Hz. The paper writes $\theta$ for $q$, $r$ for covariance, and $D$ for spatial dimension. This guide uses $q,C,d$ to avoid conflicts with earlier chapters. The original input threshold is $q\sigma_h$. In the paper's Equation 3 the firing rate is proportional to $[h-q\sigma_h]_+$, which is equivalent to this form after choosing the gain.[^p3-model]

review.purpose: Define units and map source notation to guide notation.
review.connection: Interprets the normalized firing equation before parameter comparisons.
review.reason: q, a and sigma_h have distinct roles; source symbols would otherwise collide with earlier chapters.

paragraphs.text: The input threshold summarizes how much combined input is needed before the model cell fires. It can reflect the cell's own response properties and inhibitory input. Raising $q$ at a fixed input map leaves fewer positions active. If the absolute threshold above the input mean is positive and held fixed, increasing the input standard deviation $\sigma_h$ lowers $q$, making activity more widespread. Changing $a$ instead changes rates within active regions while preserving their zero-rate boundaries. A fixed positive detection cutoff in Hz would change this last conclusion. [A fitted threshold describes the balance of input and response. It does not identify which biological quantity changed.]{.key-statement}

review.purpose: Explain threshold, input amplitude and gain effects.
review.connection: Uses the firing equation to interpret fitted parameters.
review.reason: It preserves the zero-rate-boundary condition and the limit on identifying biology.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.CataphoricForecasting = NO --> <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = NO --> Each connected piece of $A_q$ is a model place field. In one dimension its size is length. In two and three dimensions it is area and volume. [Two nearby peaks belong to one field if an above-threshold path joins them. Counting peaks and counting fields therefore answer different questions.]{.key-statement} <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = YES --> <!-- vale ai-tells.CataphoricForecasting = YES -->

review.purpose: Start the derivative-variance calculation.
review.connection: Connects covariance of inputs to slopes along the map.
review.reason: It supplies the equation from which the local scale is defined.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = NO --> Thus $\sigma$ compares typical height with typical slope and has units of distance. In an isotropic field, the same definition applies along any unit direction. For the smooth Gaussian covariance $C(\Delta x)=\sigma_h^2\exp[-\|\Delta x\|^2/(2\sigma^2)]$, it is exactly the parameter in that exponent. The paper uses a Gaussian covariance for its simulations. Other smooth covariances can share this local scale while having different longer distance structure.[^p3-scale] <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = YES -->

review.purpose: Interpret sigma as height relative to slope and limit its reach.
review.connection: Connects the formula to units and the simulation covariance.
review.reason: Equal local scales need not mean equal long-distance dependence.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.EmDashUsage = NO --> Thresholding changes the distribution of values and can separate one smooth input curve into several fields. Both panels describe the same fixed map over space, so neither curve is a trajectory over time. See [Gaussian input and firing rate, STAR Methods Eqs. 2–3, p. e1](../papers/mainali-2025-universal-statistics.pdf#page=13). <!-- vale ai-tells.EmDashUsage = YES -->

review.purpose: Interpret rectification and the spatial axes.
review.connection: Follows the teaching map and returns to field geometry.
review.reason: It states the result needed for counting without relying on the original-paper fold.

paragraphs.text: A field starts at an upcrossing, so its expected count can be found by counting upward passages through the threshold. A small interval around each crossing has a width determined by its slope. This lets us count crossings without locating every root.

review.purpose: Motivate counting through local crossing widths.
review.connection: Uses the earlier upcrossing definition to open the derivation.
review.reason: It gives the purpose before the integral.

paragraphs.text: Consider a differentiable fixed curve and a simple upward crossing $x_0$ of $q$, with slope $v=z'(x_0)>0$. Close to the crossing,

review.purpose: Set a fixed simple crossing and its positive slope.
review.connection: Prepares the local Taylor display.
review.reason: The regular crossing assumptions make the narrow-band argument meaningful.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.EmDashUsage = NO --> The curve lies in the vertical band $|z-q|<\varepsilon$ for a spatial distance approximately $2\varepsilon/v$. Integrating $z'(x)/(2\varepsilon)$ over that interval contributes one. Restricting to positive slopes counts only upward crossings. [Under the usual regularity conditions, averaging this counting identity gives the [**Kac–Rice formula**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} for the mean upcrossing density,]{.definition-explanation} <!-- vale ai-tells.EmDashUsage = YES -->

review.purpose: Turn a band width into one count and then an expected density.
review.connection: Uses the linear crossing display to derive slope weighting.
review.reason: It connects the geometric operation to the Kac–Rice name.

paragraphs.text: The density $p_{z,z'}(q,v)$ describes how often height is near $q$ and slope near $v$. Multiplication by $v$ compensates for the shorter spatial window of a steep crossing. Multiplying the probability of being above threshold by a typical slope would miss this weighting.[^p3-crossings]

For a unit direction in an isotropic field it has the same local length scale $\sigma$. The same argument applies to a flat plane. paragraphs.text: Choosing one original field uniformly and cutting through its centre is different from choosing lines uniformly through space. Large fields are more likely to be hit by a spatially sampled line, and most hits pass away from their centres. The Gaussian restriction argument describes excursions along the sampled line. The radius distribution for fields counted once each cannot be used directly as the distribution of lengths observed along a line. In the high peak picture, an isotropic $d$ dimensional field has a radius of order $\sigma/q$. Converting this same radius into $d$ dimensional size and then cutting it requires both hit probability and cut position.

review.purpose: Explain hit and cut-position bias.
review.connection: Limits the use of the equal-field radius distribution.

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = NO --> Now include the boundary of an ordinary closed square or cube of side $L$, whose opposite faces are not joined and with every intersecting component retained. On a $j$ dimensional face, derivatives along the face give the same calculation as above. Each of its $d-j$ gradient components perpendicular to the face and directed out of the box must have the appropriate sign to contribute to the boundary Morse count. Symmetry and independence give a factor $2^{-(d-j)}$. There are $2^{d-j}\binom dj$ such faces, each of size $L^j$. Their combined coefficient is therefore $\binom djL^j$. Corners supply $Q(q)$ in total. With $r=L/\sigma$, the formulas become <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = YES -->

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.EmDashUsage = NO --> These reproduce the paper's Equations 8–10 for interval, square, and cube geometry. They are not the formulas for a periodic box. For a rectangle or rectangular room, replace $2L$ or $3L$ by the sum of side lengths, $3L^2$ by the sum of pairwise side products, and $L^3$ by volume. A general domain requires its own geometric boundary factors. Applying only the volume term to a small room would discard real boundary contributions. <!-- vale ai-tells.EmDashUsage = YES -->

paragraphs.text: <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = NO --> Figure 1C distinguishes a limiting analytical Rayleigh curve from the finite threshold simulation histogram. paragraphs.text: For a circuit representing position, three questions arise:

review.purpose: Introduce three questions for a position-representing circuit.

paragraphs.text: **Spatial map:** What activity pattern corresponds to each position? The place-field model addresses this question.

review.purpose: Identify the map question.
review.connection: First object in the comparison.
review.reason: It separates tuning from motion of the represented value.

paragraphs.text: **Memory motion:** How does the represented position evolve when there is no corrective input? The persistent-activity model addresses this question.

review.purpose: Identify the memory-motion question.
review.connection: Contrasts dynamics with p15's fixed mapping.
review.reason: The no-correction condition defines the relevant memory regime.

paragraphs.text: **Observed movement:** How does a downstream physical system transform that changing signal into an observable movement? The eye-drift model combines a candidate account of memory motion with a detailed account of this transformation.[^s-three]

review.purpose: Identify the downstream movement question.

review.reason: Motor transformation is not identical to state dynamics.

paragraphs.text: The objects differ even when the word position appears in all three. In 2012, $\theta(t)$ locates a network state on its attractor. In 2022, the internal eye-position command and actual eye angle are separate quantities linked through motor neurons and mechanics. In 2025, $x$ locates an animal in an environment, and $h_i(x)$ is a spatial input function assigned to a cell. The Gaussian process does not update a remembered $x$ through time.

review.purpose: Map the word position to each paper's object.
review.connection: Explains why the three questions cannot be merged by notation.
review.reason: Network coordinate, command, physical angle and animal location differ.

paragraphs.text: The 2012 and 2022 connection is direct: neural noise can move a maintained eye-position command, which then drives muscles. The 2022 result provides evidence for a substantial shared source before the final motor neurons and shows that integrator diffusion is sufficient within the constructed model. It does not measure the circuit's Fisher information or test equality in the 2012 bound. The place-field model describes spatially irregular tuning curves. To connect those curves to memory dynamics, we must also specify how the represented position moves.

review.purpose: State the direct eye-memory connection and the missing spatial-time link.
review.connection: Interprets the table and motivates the following construction.
review.reason: The 2022 evidence does not measure the 2012 information bound's equality.

paragraphs.text: The shared-position calculation predicts how rates would change together. Establishing that connection requires measurements of those changes as well as the spatial maps. Each paper tests a different part of the proposed connection:

paragraphs.text: **Place-field statistics:** A model that matches one distribution may have enough adjustable parameters to do so for several different reasons. The place-field paper gains support by fitting arrangement parameters and then comparing additional features, including slices and shape statistics. The separate firing-rate multiplier used in some comparisons should remain visible when counting how many quantities were predicted without further fitting. A successful high-threshold formula is also a statement about its limiting assumptions. Finite-threshold simulations and the original recordings provide different kinds of checks.

review.purpose: Separate place-model fits, extra statistics and approximation tests.
review.connection: First evidential comparison.
review.reason: Gain fitting and finite-q checks prevent overcounting predictions.

paragraphs.text: **Eye drift:** The eye paper calibrates a movement-to-firing relationship, inverts it, and compares the resulting single-neuron displacement predictions with measured displacement. Shared covariance then carries information that independent private fluctuations cannot supply under the decomposition's assumptions. The additional MSD comparison tests the time structure: increasing stationary motor-noise amplitude cannot by itself reproduce the accumulating upstream signal. Calibration validity, source correlations, two animals, and horizontal movement remain part of the result's scope. <!-- vale ai-tells.VerbTricolon = YES --> <!-- vale ai-tells.FigurativeCarries = YES -->

review.purpose: Separate shared-drive evidence from timing-model interpretation.
review.connection: Second evidential comparison after spatial tests.
review.reason: Calibration, decomposition and sample scope remain visible.

paragraphs.text: **Memory stability:** The 2012 inequality is a mathematical constraint rather than an experimental fit. Its derivation specifies what noise and dynamics it covers. An experimental comparison would need estimates of diffusion, the relevant time constants, and the appropriate instantaneous information rate, all under compatible conditions. Agreement with $1/N$ scaling alone would not test the entire inequality, since several mechanisms can share that scaling. <!-- vale ai-tells.VerbTricolon = YES -->

review.purpose: State what testing the memory bound would require.
review.connection: Third comparison distinguishes a mathematical inequality from a fit.
review.reason: A common 1/N scaling does not establish its full coefficient or equality.

paragraphs.text: Related studies test the assumptions and ask questions the three papers leave open:

review.purpose: Introduce related work by its effect on assumptions and open questions.
review.connection: Continues the evidence limits rather than opening an unrelated reading list.
review.reason: The following groups answer the promised relationship.

paragraphs.text: **Integrating movement:** The eye-position account begins with Seung's line-attractor model. Aksay and colleagues then used recordings and perturbations in goldfish to constrain integrator circuitry. These establish the dynamical problem and experimental architecture behind the 2022 model. Neither supplies the macaque displacement-variance estimate. Burak and Fiete's earlier grid-cell study examines [[**path integration**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}, updating a position estimate from movement.]{.definition-explanation} In its model, velocity drives recurrent population activity, and errors accumulate in the position estimate. Its accuracy ranges belong to the simulated networks and parameter choices, rather than all biological grid circuits.[^s-attractors]

review.purpose: Connect line attractors, circuit perturbation and path integration.
review.connection: First related group extends the dynamics story.
review.reason: Different species and models are not substituted for the macaque variance estimate.

paragraphs.text: **Storage capacity and changing synapses:** Noise-driven storage also connects to memory capacity. Koyluoglu and colleagues ask how noise limits recall as the delay and number of stored items increase. Their comparison with human data shows why direct storage of several independent values need not capture observed behavior. Transformations before and after storage alter the performance prediction. Seeholzer and colleagues examine how short-term changes in synaptic strength affect diffusion and systematic drift. These papers change the storage assumptions rather than invalidate the 2012 calculation inside its original model.[^s-extensions]

review.purpose: Explain storage-transform and synaptic-dynamics extensions.
review.connection: Adds changes in assumptions after the baseline circuit accounts.
review.reason: These extensions need not contradict the original theorem within its model.

paragraphs.text: **Recordings from larger environments:** For place fields, Eliav and colleagues' long-tunnel recordings and Harland and colleagues' large-arena recordings supply the multiple-field, multiple-scale observations. Yartsev and Ulanovsky supply the three-dimensional bat recordings. The 2025 paper reanalyzes those existing data, so its agreement across dimensions is not three newly collected experiments under one protocol. The later study by Maimon and colleagues directly compares CA3 and CA1 in large tunnels: predominantly single fields in CA3 contrast with multiple fields in CA1, while field sizes are similar. That distinction supports treating the CA1 statistics and the upstream spatial circuit as related but separately constrained parts of the explanation.[^s-place-data]

review.purpose: Identify reused spatial datasets and the newer CA3/CA1 constraint.
review.connection: Connects spatial statistics to their recording sources.
review.reason: Reanalysis and new cross-region data have different evidential roles.

paragraphs.text: **Connectivity and learning:** Gaussian spatial statistics do not identify a unique pattern of connections. Druckmann and colleagues report structured synaptic connectivity between hippocampal regions. Bittner and colleagues show how electrical events in [[**dendrite**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}s, the branching input structures of neurons,]{.definition-explanation} can induce changes in synaptic strength and form CA1 place fields. Structure and learning can therefore be present even when a random-function model describes many aggregate field statistics. The model's success leaves open which circuit mechanism produces these maps. Input, connectivity, learning, or perturbation measurements could distinguish the possibilities.[^s-wiring] <!-- vale ai-tells.FormalTransitions = YES -->

review.purpose: Use connectivity and plasticity studies to limit circuit uniqueness.
review.connection: Follows the spatial-input question with direct circuit evidence.
review.reason: Dendrites are defined where their causal role first matters.

paragraphs.text: **Benefits for perception:** The source and use of eye motion are different questions. Nghiem and colleagues combine human eye tracking with a model of how eye movement affects visual signals to explain why an intermediate amount of fixational motion can help fine visual discrimination. A movement that partly originates from internal noise can still have useful sensory consequences, and feedback can regulate its statistics. Benefit for perception does not uniquely identify the neural generator.[^s-acuity]

review.purpose: Separate the cause of eye motion from its sensory benefit.
review.connection: Closes related work with a distinct function question.
review.reason: Useful sensory motion does not by itself identify the generator.

review.reason: The proposed observation matches the shared-coordinate calculation.
